title: Hotfix: reduce stage-tagged metrics cardinality after Dedicated rollout stage tagging
author: Caleb Johnson
description:
Context: PR #28521 introduced stage identifiers on key request metrics/traces so gate evaluation and Console evidence panels can attribute signals per Dedicated rollout stage. After enabling this behind the beta feature flag, we observed a metrics cardinality jump (Prometheus series count + memory pressure) due to stage_id being attached to a few high-volume metric families that already include several other labels (route/model/region/pool). This hotfix reduces label cardinality while preserving gate correctness and debuggability.

What changed:
- Introduced a stricter label allowlist for "stage-aware" metrics. Only a small set of gate-critical metrics keep a stage dimension (error_rate, request_drop/429, latency histograms used by gates, saturation/headroom gauges).
- Replaced high-cardinality `rollout_stage_id` with a stable, low-cardinality `rollout_stage_key` (e.g. "s01_1pct", "s02_10pct", "s03_50pct", "s04_100pct"). Stage keys are derived from the plan stage ordinal + traffic split bucket, not UUIDs.
- Dropped stage labels entirely from per-route/per-model request counters and from verbose breakdown metrics that are primarily used for ad-hoc analytics.
- Tracing: keep full `rollout_stage_id` as a span attribute only when the span is sampled (so we still have deep-debug paths without multiplying metric series). Non-sampled spans only carry `rollout_stage_key`.
- Added guardrails: if the stage key cannot be computed (missing plan/stage mapping), emit `rollout_stage_key="unknown"` rather than falling back to UUIDs.
- Updated internal dashboard queries and gate-evidence query templates in this repo to use `rollout_stage_key` where applicable, and removed stage breakdowns from panels that were not gate-related.

Why this is safe:
- Gate evaluation queries (policy engine) only require a consistent per-stage partition key; they do not require a UUID label.
- Rollout auditability is preserved via control-plane audit events and trace attributes (sampled), not by high-cardinality metric labels.

Operational notes:
- No migrations.
- Rollback: safe to revert; but if reverting after this hotfix, dashboards/templates expecting `rollout_stage_key` will break until reverted as well.
- Post-deploy verification: check Prometheus series count for `redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket{rollout_stage_key!=""}` and confirm series count returns to baseline; confirm gate evidence still renders for beta pools.

Follow-ups:
- Add a CI check that asserts series-count bounds for stage-tagged metrics (proposal in ENG-5966 follow-up).
- Coordinate with Observability Pack to mirror query changes where dashboards are sourced externally.
commits: telemetry: introduce stage tag policy + allowlist for metric families
metrics: replace rollout_stage_id label with rollout_stage_key buckets
tracing: move full stage_id to sampled span attrs only
dashboards: update stage panels to use rollout_stage_key; remove non-gate stage breakdowns
tests: add unit coverage for stage label emission + unknown-stage behavior
notable_snippet:
Before: redwood_request_total{account_id,pool_id,region,route,model,rollout_stage_id,...}
After:  redwood_request_total{account_id,pool_id,region,route,model,...}  (no stage label)
Gate metrics keep: rollout_stage_key (bucketed), region, pool_id
Tracing keeps: rollout_stage_id only on sampled spans
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we quantify the series reduction expected? Also please confirm we are not breaking the SLO/gate dashboards that were just rolled out.

Caleb Johnson (author): With this change, stage becomes a 4-6 value bucket per rollout plan instead of UUID per stage, and we remove it from per-route/per-model counters. In staging, `prometheus_tsdb_head_series` dropped ~18% and the top offender metric family (`redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket`) dropped from ~2.1M -> ~0.6M series at peak. I updated the in-repo dashboard templates + gate query drafts to use `rollout_stage_key`.
Logan Wright: +1 on bucketed key. Please make sure we never fall back to UUIDs if mapping is missing; use "unknown" and alert separately. Also can we keep full stage_id somewhere for debugging?

Caleb Johnson (author): Added `unknown` fallback and a counter `rollout_stage_key_unknown_total` (no extra labels) so we can detect mapping issues. Full `rollout_stage_id` is now only on sampled span attributes (`rollout.stage_id`).
Mina Haddad: Any risk that routing emits different stage key values across regions for the same plan? This needs to be deterministic for multi-region pools.

Caleb Johnson (author): Stage key derivation is from plan stage ordinal + configured split bucket, sourced from control-plane plan payload; same across regions. Added a test to assert stable encoding.
Peter Holtz: For hotfixes we generally want a clear roll-forward plan. Is there any need for a staged deploy / feature flag here?

Caleb Johnson (author): No new flags; this reduces label cardinality universally and is backward-compatible for gates (they use templates we updated). Roll-forward is preferred; rollback instructions are in the PR body.
Allison Grant: Please also remove stage breakdown from any dashboards that are not used for promotion gating to prevent accidental re-introduction of cardinality pressure via copied queries.
Caleb Johnson (author): Done; removed stage grouping on route-level panels and kept it only on the stage gate overview.
Logan Wright: Approved once CI is green and you add a short note in release notes / #eng-oncall about expected metrics changes.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added release note blurb to internal changelog entry and posted in #eng-oncall (link in internal comment).
release_notes: Reduced telemetry metrics cardinality for Dedicated staged rollouts by replacing `rollout_stage_id` with bucketed `rollout_stage_key` and limiting stage labels to gate-critical metrics.
Dashboards/templates updated accordingly; full stage UUID retained in sampled traces only.
